title: STOP assembles to 0x00
rationale: STOP is in the assembler table and must keep its Yellow Paper opcode.

rationale: ADD is in the assembler table and must keep its Yellow Paper opcode.

title: push_u 0 is PUSH0
rationale: Shanghai allows PUSH0. The assembler selects it for zero.

title: PUSH width boundaries
rationale: 1 and 255 are PUSH1, 256 and 65535 are PUSH2, 65536 is PUSH3.

title: 256 is PUSH2
rationale: 256 does not fit in PUSH1.

title: 65535 is PUSH2
rationale: The PUSH2 maximum.

title: 65536 is PUSH3
rationale: 65536 crosses the PUSH2 boundary.

title: 2^256-1 is PUSH32
rationale: The largest unsigned 256-bit immediate is 33 bytes with opcode 0x7f.

title: Negative push is rejected
rationale: PUSH immediates are unsigned unless a future spec says otherwise.

title: Values wider than 32 bytes are rejected
rationale: 2^256 must not be encoded as opcode 0x80.

title: A raw byte after PUSH1 is rejected
rationale: Loose immediates desynchronize later passes. Rejection is the normative result.

title: SHR is reported as an unknown opcode
rationale: The codegen emits SHR, but the assembler must not invent a byte for an unlisted opcode.

title: SHL is an unknown opcode
rationale: Observed assembler behavior for an opcode the codegen emits.

title: GAS is an unknown opcode
rationale: Observed assembler behavior for an opcode the codegen emits.

title: Nested instruction lists flatten
rationale: The assembler documents that lists are flattened.

title: Duplicate labels are rejected
rationale: Two definitions of one label are ambiguous.

title: Undefined labels are a structured error
rationale: A jump to a missing label must not be a KeyError.

title: Forward jump assembles under the watchdog
rationale: Historic left_pad recursion must finish and land on JUMPDEST.

title: JUMPI placeholder size matches the encoding
rationale: Pass 1 currently counts 3 bytes and pass 2 writes 4. The hang masks the measurement.
note: Normative size is PUSH1 imm + PUSH2 addr + JUMPI + JUMPDEST + STOP once left_pad returns. 6 bytes assumes the pushed 1 is PUSH1. Re-measure if the jump width fix changes the address width.

title: Every assembler opcode keeps its Yellow Paper byte
rationale: One vector covers each atom in @opcode_map. A wrong or missing byte fails this case.

title: Dispatcher compares a duplicated selector
rationale: PUSH selector, DUP1, then compare to the first calldata word. Dropping DUP1 consumes the selector.

title: Calldata shorter than a selector is the failure condition
rationale: CALLDATASIZE, PUSH1 4, LT. A true result must revert before dispatch.

title: CALL arguments are pushed then CALL
rationale: Seven stack items then CALL: gas, address, value, args offset, args size, ret offset, ret size. GAS and PUSH20 are the production forms; this vector locks the order with opcodes the assembler already accepts.

title: Return data shorter than a word is the failure condition
rationale: RETURNDATASIZE, PUSH1 32, LT. A true result is not a successful ERC-20 return.

title: Forward jump lands on JUMPDEST at PC 255
rationale: Address 255 still fits in PUSH1. Pass 1 and pass 2 must agree, and byte 255 must be JUMPDEST.

title: Forward jump lands on JUMPDEST at PC 256
rationale: Address 256 requires PUSH2. The recorded PC must be 256, not the pass-1 estimate.

title: Backward jump targets an earlier JUMPDEST
rationale: The label is behind the jump. The assembled immediate is that earlier PC.
